---

# 📋 Company Expense Policy Brief

**Sources:**
- **Travel and Expense Policy** — Policy No. NW-FI-006, Version 4.0, Effective 1 January 2025. Owner: Rosa Delgado, Controller. Approver: Elena Vasquez, CFO. *(company/second-synthetic/travel-and-expense-policy.md)*
- **Employee Handbook** — Version 4.2, Effective 1 January 2025. Approved by: Dana Whitfield, CEO. *(company/second-synthetic/employee-handbook.md)*

---

## 1. Guiding Principle
> *"Spend company money as if it were your own, and keep the receipt. Travel is for business, not for comfort. The cheapest reasonable option that gets the job done is the standard."*
— Travel and Expense Policy, p.1

---

## 2. Pre-Approval Requirements
Approval must be **recorded in the finance system before** any purchase or booking. A verbal approval is **not sufficient** for travel, equipment, or any purchase above $2,500 USD.

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| Under $500 | Direct manager |
| $500 – $2,499 | Direct manager **and** department head |
| $2,500 or more | Department head **and** CFO |
| International (any cost) | Department head, CFO, **and** General Counsel |

> ⚠️ If a trip is booked before approval, the traveller accepts the risk that the cost will **not** be reimbursed.

---

- **Economy class** required for flights under 6 hours.
- **Premium economy** allowed for flights of 6 hours or more.
- **Business class** requires written VP approval and is limited to flights over 9 hours.
- Book at least **14 days in advance** when the trip is known; book within 4 hours of the lowest fare shown in the travel portal.
- Change fees are reimbursable only when caused by the customer or company; personal changes are at the traveller's cost.
- Frequent flyer miles earned on company travel **belong to the traveller**.

Here is a comprehensive brief on what company policy says about expenses, drawn entirely from the internal policy documents:

---

## 📋 Company Expense Policy Brief

**Source:** Travel and Expense Policy (NW-FI-006, v4.0, effective 1 January 2025) [1][8] and Employee Handbook (v4.2) [5][24]

---

### 🧭 Guiding Principle
> *"Spend company money as if it were your own, and keep the receipt. Travel is for business, not for comfort. The cheapest reasonable option that gets the job done is the standard."* [8]

---

### ✅ Pre-Approval Requirements
- All approvals must be recorded in the finance system **before** booking or purchasing — a verbal approval is not sufficient [8][24].
- If a trip is booked before approval, the traveller accepts the risk that the cost will **not** be reimbursed [8].

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| Under $500 | Direct manager |
| $500–$2,499 | Direct manager + department head |
| $2,500 or more | Department head + CFO |
| International (any cost) | Department head, CFO, and General Counsel |

[1]

---

### ✈️ Air Travel
- **Economy class** required for flights under 6 hours [8].
- **Premium economy** allowed for flights 6 hours or more [8].
- **Business class** requires written VP approval and is limited to flights over 9 hours [8].
- Book at least **14 days in advance** when the trip is known [8].
- Change fees are reimbursable only when caused by the customer or company; personal changes are at the traveller's cost [8].
- Frequent flyer miles earned on company travel belong to the traveller [8].

---

### 🏨 Hotel / Lodging Caps (nightly, before tax)

| City Tier | Nightly Cap | Example Cities |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 (High Cost) | $320 | New York, San Francisco, Seattle, Boston, DC, Chicago |
| Tier 2 (Standard) | $220 | Portland, Denver, Austin, Atlanta, Minneapolis |
| Tier 3 (Other Domestic) | $175 | All other U.S. locations |
| International | $260 | Any location outside the U.S. |

A room above the cap requires written department head approval before booking [1][8].

---

### 🍽️ Per Diem (Meals)

| Trip Type | Per Diem Per Day |
|---|---|
| Domestic, Tier 1 or Tier 2 city | $65 |
| Domestic, Tier 3 city | $55 |
| International | $110 |
| Travel day with 8+ hours of travel | $65 (no reduction) |

[1]

Here is a comprehensive brief on what company policy says about expenses, drawn entirely from the internal policy documents:

---

## 📋 Company Expense Policy Brief

**Source:** Travel and Expense Policy (NW-FI-006, v4.0, effective 1 January 2025) [1][8] and Employee Handbook (v4.2) [5][24]

---

### 🧭 Guiding Principle
> *"Spend company money as if it were your own, and keep the receipt. Travel is for business, not for comfort. The cheapest reasonable option that gets the job done is the standard."* [8]

---

### ✅ Pre-Approval Requirements
- All approvals must be recorded in the finance system **before** booking or purchasing. A verbal approval is not sufficient. [8][24]
- If a trip is booked before approval, the traveller accepts the risk that the cost will **not** be reimbursed. [8]

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| Under $500 | Direct manager |
| $500–$2,499 | Direct manager + department head |
| $2,500 or more | Department head + CFO |
| International (any cost) | Department head, CFO, and General Counsel |

[1]

---

### ✈️ Air Travel
- **Economy class** required for flights under 6 hours. [8]
- **Premium economy** allowed for flights 6 hours or more. [8]
- **Business class** requires written VP approval and is limited to flights over 9 hours. [8]
- Book at least **14 days in advance**; book within 4 hours of the lowest fare shown in the travel portal. [8]
- Change fees are reimbursable only when caused by the customer or company; personal changes are at the traveller's cost. [8]
- Frequent flyer miles earned on company travel belong to the traveller. [8]

---

### 🏨 Hotel / Lodging Caps (nightly, before tax)

| City Tier | Nightly Cap | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 – High Cost | $320 | New York, San Francisco, Seattle, Boston, DC, Chicago |
| Tier 2 – Standard | $220 | Portland, Denver, Austin, Atlanta, Minneapolis |
| Tier 3 – Other Domestic | $175 | All other U.S. locations |
| International | $260 | Any location outside the U.S. |

A room above the cap requires written department head approval before booking. [1][8]

---

### 🍽️ Per Diem (Meals)

| Trip Type | Per Diem/Day |
|---|---|
| Domestic, Tier 1 or Tier 2 city | $65 |
| Domestic, Tier 3 city | $55 |
| International | $110 |
| Travel day with >8

I have a clear, direct answer from the documents. Here is the brief:

---

## Travel Approval Threshold Under 500 USD

**Finding:** For trips costing **under 500 USD**, the required approval is from the employee's **direct manager** only.

**Source:** This is explicitly stated in the Travel and Expense Policy (Policy No. NW-FI-006, Version 4.0, effective 1 January 2025), which contains the following approval matrix [2]:

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| **Under 500 USD** | **Direct manager** |
| 500 to 2,499 USD | Direct manager and department head |
| 2,500 USD or more | Department head and CFO |
| International, any cost | Department head, CFO, and General Counsel |

The same policy also notes that approval must be **recorded in the travel request in the finance system before booking** — a verbal approval is not sufficient [4].

---

**No irreversible actions were taken.** Only read-only document searches were performed. Please confirm if you'd like any further research or action.

Here is a comprehensive brief on what company policy says about expenses, drawn entirely from the internal policy documents:

---

## 📋 Company Expense Policy Brief

**Source:** Travel and Expense Policy (NW-FI-006, v4.0, effective 1 January 2025) [1][8] and Employee Handbook (v4.2) [5][24]

---

### 🧭 Guiding Principle
> *"Spend company money as if it were your own, and keep the receipt. Travel is for business, not for comfort. The cheapest reasonable option that gets the job done is the standard."* [8]

---

### ✅ Pre-Approval Requirements
- All approvals must be recorded in the finance system **before** booking or purchasing. A verbal approval is not sufficient. [8][24]
- If a trip is booked before approval, the traveller accepts the risk that the cost will **not** be reimbursed. [8]

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| Under $500 | Direct manager |
| $500–$2,499 | Direct manager + department head |
| $2,500 or more | Department head + CFO |
| International (any cost) | Department head, CFO, and General Counsel |

[1]

---

### ✈️ Air Travel
- **Economy class** required for flights under 6 hours. [8]
- **Premium economy** allowed for flights of 6 hours or more. [8]
- **Business class** requires written VP approval and is limited to flights over 9 hours. [8]
- Book at least **14 days in advance**; book within 4 hours of the lowest fare shown in the travel portal. [8]
- Change fees are reimbursable only when caused by the customer or company; personal changes are at the traveller's cost. [8]
- Frequent flyer miles earned on company travel belong to the traveller. [8]

---

### 🏨 Hotel / Lodging Caps (nightly, before tax)

| City Tier | Nightly Cap | Example Cities |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 (High Cost) | $320 | New York, San Francisco, Seattle, Boston, DC, Chicago |
| Tier 2 (Standard) | $220 | Portland, Denver, Austin, Atlanta, Minneapolis |
| Tier 3 (Other Domestic) | $175 | All other U.S. locations |
| International | $260 | Any location outside the U.S. |

A room above the cap requires written department head approval before booking. [1][8]

---

### 🍽️ Per Diem (Meals)

| Trip Type | Per Diem Per Day |
|---|---|
| Domestic, Tier 1 or Tier 2 city | $65 |
| Domestic, Tier 3 city | $55 |
| International | $110 |
| Travel

{"brief": "Here is a concise brief based on the evidence found:

---

## Travel Approval Threshold Under $500 USD

### Exact Threshold & Rule
**Trips costing under $500 USD require approval from the employee's direct manager only.**

This is the lowest tier in the travel approval matrix, which reads in full:

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| **Under 500 USD** | **Direct manager** |
| 500 to 2,499 USD | Direct manager and department head |
| 2,500 USD or more | Department head and CFO |
| International, any cost | Department head, CFO, and General Counsel |

---

### Sources
This threshold is confirmed in **two separate documents**:

1. **Travel and Expense Policy** (`NW-FI-006`, Version 4.0, effective 1 January 2025, owned by Rosa Delgado, Controller) — the primary policy document governing all employee and contractor travel and spending [1][4][7].

2. **Employee Handbook** — which cross-references the same approval matrix under its *Expenses, Travel and Corporate Card* section, reinforcing that approval must be recorded in the finance system before the purchase; a verbal approval is explicitly **not sufficient** [2][3].

---

## 📋 Company Policy Brief: Travel Approval Requirements

**Source documents:** Travel and Expense Policy (NW-FI-006, v4.0, effective 1 January 2025) and Employee Handbook — both at `company/second-synthetic/`.

---

### 1. Core Rule: Approval Before Booking

Approval must be **recorded in the travel request in the finance system before booking**. A verbal approval is not sufficient, and if a trip is booked before approval is obtained, the traveller accepts the risk that the cost will not be reimbursed [2]. The Employee Handbook reinforces this: "A verbal approval is not sufficient for travel, equipment or any purchase above 2,500 USD" [3].

---

### 2. Approval Thresholds by Trip Cost

The required approvers scale with the total estimated trip cost [1]:

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| Under $500 | Direct manager |
| $500 – $2,499 | Direct manager **and** department head |
| $2,500 or more | Department head **and** CFO |
| International (any cost) | Department head, CFO, **and** General Counsel |

---

### 3. Special Approval Situations

- **Business class flights:** Require **written approval from a Vice President** and are limited to flights over nine hours [2].
- **Hotel room above the nightly cap:** Requires **written approval from the department head** before booking [2].
- **Business meals above $75/attendee:** The **department head** must approve in writing before the meal [8].
- **Travel to a Level 3 or Level 4 advisory destination:** Requires **CEO approval** (section 12.2) [4].
- **Vendor-paid travel and entertainment:** Requires **written CFO approval** before it is accepted [7].
- **Cash advance for travel hardship:** Approved by the **CFO**, up to $1,000 [4].

---

### 4. Exceptions to Policy Limits

Any exception to a spending limit must be **requested in writing before the expense is incurred** and approved by the **CFO**. Exceptions are logged by Finance and reviewed quarterly; repeated exceptions by one department are escalated to the CFO [4].

---

### 5. Late Expense Report Approvals

Even after travel, approval requirements continue:
- Reports submitted **31–60 days late** require department head approval and a written reason [5].
- Reports submitted **over 60 days late** require CFO approval and may be denied [5].

---

### ⚠️ Approval Before Action Notice

No irreversible actions have been taken. All findings above are read-only research. If you need to submit a travel request, book a trip, or take any other action on behalf of an employee, please confirm before proceeding.

# Employee Expense Policy Brief
**Sources:** Travel and Expense Policy (NW-FI-006, v4.0, effective 1 Jan 2025) and Employee Handbook (v4.2, effective 1 Jan 2025)

---

## 1. 📋 Governing Principle
> *"Spend company money as if it were your own, and keep the receipt. Travel is for business, not for comfort. The cheapest reasonable option that gets the job done is the standard."* [17]

---

## 2. ✅ Pre-Trip Approval Requirements
Approval must be recorded in the finance system **before** booking. A verbal approval is not sufficient. If a trip is booked before approval, the traveller bears the risk of non-reimbursement. [17]

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| Under $500 | Direct manager |
| $500 – $2,499 | Direct manager + department head |
| $2,500 or more | Department head + CFO |
| International (any amount) | Department head + CFO + General Counsel |

[1]

---

## 3. ✈️ Air Travel
- **Economy class** for flights under 6 hours [17]
- **Premium economy** allowed for flights of 6 hours or more [17]
- **Business class** requires written VP approval; only on flights over 9 hours [17][18]
- Book at least **14 days in advance** when the trip is known; book within 4 hours of the lowest fare shown in the travel portal [17]
- Change fees reimbursable only if caused by the customer or company; personal changes are at the traveller's cost [17]
- Frequent flyer miles earned on company travel belong to the traveller [17]

---

Nightly caps (before tax) [1]:

| City Tier | Nightly Cap | Example Cities |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 – High Cost | $320 | New York, San Francisco, Seattle, Boston, Washington DC, Chicago |
| Tier 2 – Standard | $220 | Portland, Denver, Austin, Atlanta, Minneapolis |
| Tier 3 – Other Domestic | $175 | All other U.S. locations |
| International | $260 | Any location outside the U.S. |

- A room above the cap requires **written department head approval before booking** [17]
- Hotel internet is reimbursable when not included in the room rate (keep the receipt) [1]

---

Per diem rates per day [1][5]:

| Trip Type | Per Diem |
|---|---|
| Domestic – Tier 1 or Tier 2 city | $65/day |

{"brief": "Here is a comprehensive brief drawn entirely from the Employee Handbook (NW-HR-001 v4.2) and the Travel and Expense Policy (NW-FI-006 v4.0):

---

# 📋 Expenses, Travel & Corporate Card Policy Brief

---

## 1. 📅 Submission Deadlines

| Scenario | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **Standard deadline** | Submit expense report within **30 calendar days** of the last expense date [1][5] |
| **Late: 31–60 days** | Requires **department head approval** and a written reason [3] |
| **Late: over 60 days** | Requires **CFO approval** and may be **denied** [1][3] |
| **Manager approval** | Due within **5 business days** of submission [1] |
| **Finance review** | Within **3 business days** of manager approval [1] |
| **Reimbursement** | Within **10 business days** of finance approval, paid by direct deposit [1][6] |

---

## 2. 💳 Corporate Card Policy

- The card is for **business expenses only**; the card statement must be **reconciled with the expense report each month** [22].
- **Unreconciled charges older than 60 days** are escalated to the department head and may be **deducted from the next payroll** (where state law allows) [22].
- A **lost or stolen card** must be reported to the card issuer immediately and to the Controller the **same day** [9].
- The company does **not advance cash** for travel except in documented hardship cases, approved by the CFO, up to **$1,000 USD** [9].
- **Exceptions** to any spending limit must be requested **in writing before** the expense is incurred and approved by the CFO [9].

---

## 3. 🚫 Non-Reimbursable Items

The following are explicitly **not reimbursable** [1][11]:
- Alcohol (never reimbursable, even at meals)
- Minibar charges
- In-room movies
- Gym fees or spa services
- Airline club memberships
- Personal entertainment
- Traffic fines, parking tickets, and moving violations

# 📋 Expenses, Travel & Corporate Card Policy Brief

## Travel & Expense Policy Brief: Corporate Card, Cash Advances & Non-Reimbursable Expenses
**Source:** `travel-and-expense-policy.md` (Policy NW-FI-006, v4.0, effective 1 January 2025)

---

### 💳 Corporate Card Rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Eligibility** | Employees who travel **more than four times a year** receive a corporate card [3] |
| **Card ownership** | Issued in the employee's name; the **company pays the balance** [3] |
| **Permitted use** | Airfare, lodging, rental cars, and other travel costs [3] |
| **Prohibited use** | **Personal purchases are strictly prohibited** on the corporate card [3] |
| **Lost/stolen card** | Must be reported to the card issuer **immediately** and to the Controller **the same day** [1] |

---

### 💵 Cash Advances

The company **does not advance cash for travel** as a general rule. The only exception is:
- A **documented hardship**, approved by the **CFO**, for up to a maximum of **$1,000 USD** [1]

---

### 🚫 Non-Reimbursable Expenses

The following expenses are explicitly **not reimbursable** [3]:

- 🍷 **Alcohol**
- 🍫 **Minibar** charges

- 🏋️ **Gym fees**

- 🛏️ **Hotel room upgrades**
- 👫 **Any expense for a travelling companion**
- 🚗 **Premium rideshare, limousines, or black car service** (unless there is a documented safety or client reason) [3]

---

- The corporate card is a **company-paid tool for business travel only** — personal use is a policy violation [3].
- Cash advances are a **last resort**, capped at $1,000 and requiring CFO sign-off [1].

## Travel & Expense Policy Brief: Corporate Card, Cash Advances & Non-Reimbursable Expenses
**Source:** `travel-and-expense-policy.md` (Policy NW-FI-006, v4.0, effective 1 January 2025)

---

### 💳 Corporate Card Rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Eligibility** | Employees who travel **more than four times a year** receive a corporate card [3] |
| **Card ownership** | Issued in the employee's name; the **company pays the balance** [3] |

| **Prohibited use** | **Personal purchases are strictly prohibited** on the corporate card [3] |

---

### 💵 Cash Advances

The company **does not advance cash for travel** as a general rule. The only exception is:
- A **documented hardship**, approved by the **CFO**, for up to a maximum of **$1,000 USD** [1]

## Travel & Expense Policy — Key Rules (`travel-and-expense-policy.md`)

---

| Situation | Rule |

- The card statement must be **reconciled with the expense report each month** [10].

#### Lost or Stolen Card
- Report immediately to the **card issuer** and to the **Controller the same day** [12].

{"brief": "Here is a structured brief of all rules for **meals, entertainment, and client-related expenses** as found in `company/second-synthetic/travel-and-expense-policy.md`:

---

## 🍽️ Meals & Per Diem (Section 5)

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Standard approach** | Northwind pays a **per diem** instead of reimbursing individual meals. The per diem covers three meals and incidentals. [2] |
| **Full travel day** | Per diem is paid for each full day of travel. [5] |
| **First & last day** | 75% of the daily rate when travel occupies less than a full day. [5] |
| **Customer-paid or conference meals** | Reduces the per diem by **$15 per meal**, to a floor of zero. [5] |
| **Alcohol** | **Never reimbursable**, even when it appears on a customer dinner bill. [5] |

### Per Diem Rates [6]
| Trip Type | Per Diem Per Day |
|---|---|
| Domestic, Tier 1 or Tier 2 city | $65 |
| Domestic, Tier 3 city | $55 |
| International | $110 |
| Travel day with more than 8 hours of travel | $65, no reduction |

---

## 🤝 Business Meals with Customers or Candidates (Section 5.5)

- Reimbursed at **actual cost** (not per diem) with an **itemized receipt** and a **list of attendees**. [2]
- The limit is **$75 per attendee**. [2]
- Above $75 per attendee, the **department head must approve in writing before the meal**. [2]
- Tips are reimbursable up to **20% for meals that are not per diem**. [6]

---

## 🎭 Entertainment & Non-Reimbursable Items

The following are **explicitly not reimbursable** [2]:
- Alcohol
- Minibar charges
- In-room movies
- Gym fees / spa services
- Airline club membership
- **Personal entertainment**
- Hotel room upgrades
- Any expense for a travelling companion
- Traffic fines / parking tickets

---

## 🧾 Receipt Requirements

- A receipt is required for every expense of **$25 or more**. [2]
- Below $25, a description and date are still required. [2]
- Receipts must show the merchant, date, amount, and items purchased — a credit card slip alone is **not** sufficient. [2]
- Missing receipts require a **signed missing receipt statement** from the department head. More than **3 missing receipts in a rolling 12 months** triggers a Controller review. [2]

---

---

# 📋 Expenses, Travel & Corporate Card Policy Brief

**Sources:** Employee Handbook (NW-HR-001 v4.2) [1][10][13][16][18] and Travel & Expense Policy (NW-FI-006 v4.0) [9][11][12][14][22]

---

## 1. 📅 Submission Deadlines

| Scenario | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **Standard submission** | Within **30 calendar days** of the last expense date [5][2] |
| **Late: 31–60 days** | Requires **department head approval** and a written reason [3][1] |
| **Late: 60+ days** | Requires **CFO approval**; may be **denied entirely** [3][1] |
| **Manager approval** | Due within **5 business days** of submission [1] |
| **Finance review** | Within **3 business days** after manager approval [1] |
| **Reimbursement** | Within **10 business days** of finance approval, paid by direct deposit [6][1] |

---

## 📋 Company Policy Brief: Travel Approval Requirements

**Source:** Travel and Expense Policy, Policy No. NW-FI-006, Version 4.0, effective 1 January 2025. Owner: Rosa Delgado, Controller; Approver: Elena Vasquez, CFO. Applies to all employees and contractors who travel or spend company money [1].

---

### 1. Pre-Trip Approval Is Mandatory

Approval must be **recorded in the travel request in the finance system before booking**. A verbal approval is not sufficient. If a trip is booked before approval is obtained, the traveller accepts the risk that the cost will not be reimbursed [2]. The Employee Handbook reinforces this: "A verbal approval is not sufficient for travel, equipment or any purchase above 2,500 USD" [3].

---

### 2. Approval Thresholds by Trip Cost

The required approvers scale with the total estimated trip cost [1]:

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| Under $500 | Direct manager |
| $500 – $2,499 | Direct manager **and** department head |
| $2,500 or more | Department head **and** CFO |
| International (any cost) | Department head, CFO, **and** General Counsel |

---

### 3. Special Approval Situations

- **Business class flights:** Require **written approval from a Vice President** and are limited to flights over nine hours [2].
- **Hotel room above the nightly cap:** Requires **written approval from the department head** before booking [2].
- **Business meals above $75/attendee:** The **department head must approve in writing** before the meal [8].
- **Travel to a Level 3 or Level 4 advisory destination:** Requires **CEO approval** (section 12.2) [4].
- **Vendor-paid travel and entertainment:** Requires **written CFO approval** before it is accepted [7].
- **Cash advance for travel hardship:** Requires **CFO approval**, capped at $1,000 [4].

---

### 4. Late Expense Report Submission

Even after travel, approvals continue to apply [5]:

| Submission Timing | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| 31–60 days late | Department head approval + written reason |
| Over 60 days late | CFO approval; may be denied |

---

### 5. Safety & Emergency Registration

All travellers must register every trip in the travel portal so the company can reach them in an emergency. The after-hours operations line is 503-555-0155 [4].

---

### ⚠️ Approval Before Action

No irreversible actions have been taken. This is a read-only research brief. Please review and approve before any further steps are taken.

## 📋 Travel Approval Threshold Brief

### Finding

For trips costing **under 500 USD**, only **direct manager approval** is required.

This threshold is part of a tiered approval structure:

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| **Under 500 USD** | Direct manager |
| 500 to 2,499 USD | Direct manager **and** department head |
| 2,500 USD or more | Department head **and** CFO |
| International (any cost) | Department head, CFO, **and** General Counsel |

- Approval must be **recorded in the finance system before booking** — a verbal approval is not sufficient [1][3].
- If a trip is booked before approval is obtained, the traveller accepts the risk that the cost will **not be reimbursed** [7].

- **Primary source:** `travel-and-expense-policy.md` (Policy NW-FI-006, Version 4.0, Effective 1 January 2025, Owner: Rosa Delgado, Controller) [1][4][7]

## 📋 Company Policy Brief: Travel Approval

**Sources:** Travel and Expense Policy (NW-FI-006, v4.0, effective 1 January 2025) and Employee Handbook — both from `company/second-synthetic/`

---

### 1. Core Approval Requirement

Approval **must be recorded in the travel request in the finance system before booking**. A verbal approval is not sufficient [2]. If a trip is booked before approval is obtained, the traveller accepts the risk that the cost **will not be reimbursed** [2]. The Employee Handbook reinforces this: *"A verbal approval is not sufficient for travel, equipment or any purchase above 2,500 USD"* [3].

---

### 2. Approval Authority by Trip Cost

| Trip Cost | Approval Required |
|---|---|
| Under $500 USD | Direct manager |
| $500 – $2,499 USD | Direct manager **and** department head |
| $2,500 USD or more | Department head **and** CFO |
| International (any cost) | Department head, CFO, **and** General Counsel |

[1]

---

### 3. Special Approval Situations

- **Business class flights:** Require **written approval from a Vice President** and are limited to flights over 9 hours [2].
- **Hotel rooms above the nightly cap:** Require **written approval from the department head** before booking [2].
- **Travel to a Level 3 or Level 4 advisory destination:** Requires **CEO approval** [4].
- **Business meals above $75/attendee:** Require **department head written approval** before the meal [8].
- **Vendor-paid travel and entertainment:** Requires **written CFO approval** before it is accepted [7].
- **Cash advances for travel:** Only for documented hardship, approved by the **CFO**, up to $1,000 USD [4].

---

### 4. Late Expense Report Approvals

Even after travel, late submissions require escalated approval [5]:
- **31–60 days late:** Department head approval + written reason.
- **Over 60 days late:** CFO approval; may be denied.

---

### 5. Policy Exceptions

Any exception to a policy limit must be **requested in writing before the expense is incurred** and approved by the **CFO**. Exceptions are logged by Finance and reviewed quarterly [4].

---
